title: Bijectivity of scalar extension of twisted Galois matrix invariants
statement: Let K be a field, S its separable closure, n any natural number and b:Gal(S/K) → GL_n(S) locally constant for the Krull topology. Put T_g(M)=b(g) g(M) b(g) inverse. Assume T_1(M)=M and T_g(T_h(M))=T_(gh)(M) for all g,h,M. Then the explicit multiplication map S tensor_K A_b → Mat_n(S) of [def-sc-matrix-descent-invariants] is bijective. There is no positivity assumption on n and no central simplicity assertion.

proof.text: Compactness of Gal(S/K) and local constancy give a finite image for b and an open normal subgroup N on whose cosets b is constant. Intersect N with open normal subgroups fixing all entries in the finitely many values of b and their inverses. Put L=S^N. It is finite Galois over K, and all b-values have entries in L.

The identity law says b(1) commutes with every matrix. Thus for g in N, b(g)=b(1) and T_g(M)=g(M). An invariant matrix has entries in L. On Mat_n(L) the given action factors through Gamma=Gal(L/K), since T_g acts trivially for g in N. Its invariant K-subalgebra is exactly A_b of [def-sc-matrix-descent-invariants].

For v in Mat_n(L) and a in L, sum g(a)T_g(v) over Gamma. Semilinearity and the action law imply that applying T_h reindexes by g ↦ hg, so this sum is invariant. If the L-span of invariant vectors were proper, a nonzero L-linear functional lambda would annihilate it. For each fixed v the sum of lambda(T_g(v)) g(a) vanishes for all a. Independence of distinct automorphisms implies all coefficients vanish, in particular lambda(v)=0 because T_1=id. This contradicts lambda being nonzero.

Select an L-basis consisting of invariant vectors. If a linear combination is invariant, uniqueness of its coefficients forces each coefficient to be fixed by Gamma, hence in K. Therefore the same family is a K-basis of A_b. Multiplication L tensor_K A_b → Mat_n(L) sends the extended basis to that basis. Extending scalars to S proves bijectivity of the explicit map in [def-sc-matrix-descent-invariants]. For n=0 both source and target are zero, and the empty basis gives the same conclusion.

lean.statement:
theorem matrixDescentScalarMap_bijective (K : Type u) [Field K]
    (n : ℕ)
    (b : (SeparableClosure K ≃ₐ[K] SeparableClosure K) →
      Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin n) (SeparableClosure K))
    (hb : IsLocallyConstant b)
    (h1 : ∀ M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (SeparableClosure K),
      (b 1).val * M * ((b 1)⁻¹).val = M)
    (hm : ∀ g h (M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) (SeparableClosure K)),
      (b g).val * ((b h).val * M.map h * ((b h)⁻¹).val).map g * ((b g)⁻¹).val =
        (b (g * h)).val * M.map (g * h) * ((b (g * h))⁻¹).val) :
    Function.Bijective (matrixDescentScalarMap K n b)
